items.explanation: 71-year-old man (DOB 1955-08-23) with atrial fibrillation documented 2025-08-22 (ICD-9 427.31) and carried in every cardiology clinic note through 2026-07-28. CHA2DS2-VASc 3 (age 65-74 = 1, hypertension = 1, vascular disease/coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery = 1); guideline recommends oral anticoagulation at score >=2 in men. No anticoagulant has ever been ordered - the only current medication is tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily. Needs review for initiation of anticoagulation.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2025-11-10 (first appearance in the note medication list). The 9/1/2025 memo applies because the start was before 3/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 30 days, i.e. by 2025-12-10. ECG 106885519 was recorded on 2025-11-24, 14 days after the start, so the requirement was met. (The ECG showed QTc about 531 ms - see the separate QT safety item.)

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-02-12. The start predates 3/1/2026, so the 9/1/2025 memo's 30-day window applies: ECG due by 2026-03-14. ECG 101538691 was obtained on 2026-03-08, within 30 days, so the requirement was completed. That ECG showed sinus rhythm at 68/min with QTc about 445 ms (below the 500 ms review threshold).

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-03-02. Because the start is on/after 3/1/2026 the revised memo applies and an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-03-16. ECG 104882441 was recorded on 2026-03-07, five days after the start, so the requirement was completed; it showed sinus rhythm at 81/min with QTc about 375 ms.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-04-10. Under the revised 3/1/2026 memo an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-04-24. No ECG was performed in that window; the only ECG in the chart, 107859369, was recorded on 2026-04-29 - 19 days after the start and five days after the deadline - so the requirement was not met within the required time and is overdue as of the 2026-09-24 evaluation.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started as an outpatient at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-01 (it was absent from the medication list at the 2026-06-24 visit and appears for the first time on 2026-08-01). Under the revised 3/1/2026 memo an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-08-15. No ECG has been obtained since 2025-12-25 (106035722), so the requirement is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-10, so under the revised 3/1/2026 memo an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-08-24. No ECG exists in the chart for this patient. However the nurse telephone note of 2026-08-25 (DocumentReference/5e12a8aa-0439-53cd-a194-cc1a277d296d) records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 8/18 - inside the required window - and that the report was requested by fax but not yet received. That outside tracing could satisfy the requirement, so the status cannot be determined until the report is obtained.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-15; it is new to the medication list at that visit. Under the revised 3/1/2026 memo an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-09-29. No ECG has been done since 2025-03-09 (104253928). As of the 2026-09-24 evaluation the requirement is not yet due, but the ECG must be obtained in the next five days.

At the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-01 Dr Paul Kessler documented 'INR today 1.6, subtherapeutic. Increase warfarin to 7.5 mg daily; recheck INR' - a warfarin dose change made by a clinic clinician after the 3/1/2026 effective date, so an INR was required within 7 days (by 2026-09-08). INR 2.3 was resulted on 2026-09-05 (Observation d6b3bad5), four days after the change, so the monitoring requirement was completed.

Anticoagulation clinic telephone note of 2026-09-10 by L. Nguyen, PharmD: 'Home INR 3.4. Warfarin decreased from 5 mg to 4 mg daily per protocol.' A clinic pharmacist is authorised to adjust warfarin under the 6/1/2024 standing order, so this is a qualifying dose change and an INR was required within 7 days, by 2026-09-17. The most recent INR in the chart is 2.6 from 2026-08-22; no INR has been resulted since the dose change, so the requirement is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

71-year-old woman (DOB 1955-09-07) with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (ICD-10 I48.0) documented during the 2025-03-14 admission for embolic cerebral infarction. CHA2DS2-VASc 5: female sex 1, age 65-74 1, hypertension 1, prior stroke 2. Guideline recommends oral anticoagulation. No anticoagulant is ordered - current medications per the 2026-07-10 clinic note are carvedilol, metoprolol tartrate and famotidine only, and no anticoagulant appears anywhere in the medication record. Needs review for initiation of anticoagulation for secondary stroke prevention.

Outside-records summary of 2026-08-12 documents an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 to Mercy Hospital for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9, 2 units transfused) with apixaban held at discharge pending cardiology review. That review has not happened: at the 2026-08-20 clinic visit apixaban 5 mg twice daily was re-ordered (valid 2026-08-20 to 2026-12-28) and the note states 'continue current regimen', with concurrent aspirin 81 mg and clopidogrel 75 mg. A current anticoagulant (plus dual antiplatelet therapy) is therefore running despite a documented major GI bleed that was explicitly flagged as requiring review before resumption.

Two oral anticoagulants are current for this patient with paroxysmal/persistent atrial fibrillation. At the 2026-07-15 cardiology clinic visit the plan was to switch rivaroxaban to apixaban ('Switching anticoagulant from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage. Start apixaban 5 mg twice daily'), but rivaroxaban 20 mg daily was re-ordered the same day (valid 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-25) alongside the new apixaban 5 mg twice daily order (valid 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-26), and the note's own medication list shows both drugs. Rivaroxaban was never discontinued, so as of 2026-09-24 the patient has overlapping apixaban and rivaroxaban - a major bleeding hazard requiring immediate reconciliation.

The clinic note of 2026-06-10 10:55 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that same day contradict this: 107914094 (2026-06-10 17:13) shows an irregularly irregular rhythm at a mean ventricular rate of about 133/min with no discernible P waves, and 103088543 (2026-06-10 19:36) shows the same at about 136/min - i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, not sinus rhythm at 72. Unspecified atrial fibrillation was in fact coded at the 2026-06-10/12 encounter and warfarin was started. The documented rhythm and rate need correction and the rate-control/anticoagulation plan re-reviewed.

Patient is on escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug per the 1/15/2025 QT monitoring memo), most recently re-ordered 2026-04-23 and current. His most recent ECG, 108018814 of 2023-10-08, shows sinus rhythm at 68/min with QT about 490 ms and a Bazett-corrected QTc of about 520 ms (>=500 ms), driven by a markedly prolonged ST segment and late broad T wave. Notably the 2024-05-14 note that started escitalopram described this same ECG as 'QT acceptable'. Prescriber review of escitalopram is required; potassium 4.1 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (2025-08-23) are normal, so a repeat ECG and drug review are indicated.

Patient is on citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch-list drug), current order 2026-05-29 to 2026-12-25. Her most recent ECG, 104821039 of 2023-11-10, shows sinus rhythm at 70/min with QT about 505 ms and QTc (Bazett) about 548 ms, well above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT monitoring memo; QTc had risen from 416 ms on the previous ECG (107149156, 2020-06-17). Citalopram at 40 mg is above the dose recommended when QT prolongation is a concern. Potassium 4.5 mEq/L (2026-01-21) and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (2023-12-01) are normal. Prescriber review of citalopram dose and a repeat ECG are required.

Patient with atrial fibrillation is on amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list drug), current order 2026-07-29 to 2027-01-05. His most recent ECG, 106885519 of 2025-11-24, shows sinus rhythm at 62/min with QT about 515 ms and QTc (Bazett) about 531 ms, i.e. >=500 ms; QTc rose from 414 ms on the preceding ECG (108780865, 2025-06-07) after amiodarone was started at the 2025-11-10 clinic visit. Potassium 4.4 mEq/L and magnesium 2.2 mg/dL (2026-04-20) are normal. Prescriber review of amiodarone is required per the clinic QT monitoring memo.

95-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation/flutter on amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list drug), current order 2026-08-22 to 2027-01-05, together with warfarin and metoprolol. Her most recent ECG, 101515306 of 2022-04-27, shows sinus rhythm at 58/min with QT about 550 ms and QTc (Bazett) about 542 ms, i.e. >=500 ms (QTc was 453 ms on the preceding ECG 100867733 three weeks earlier, when she was in atrial fibrillation). Magnesium is low-normal at 1.8 mg/dL with potassium 4.1 mEq/L (2026-02-14). No ECG has been obtained since 2022 despite continuous amiodarone; prescriber review and a current ECG are required.

interpretations.explanation: Sinus rhythm at 81/min with a clear upright P wave in II/III/aVF (negative in aVL) preceding every QRS; RR intervals vary smoothly (329-429 samples) as respiratory sinus variation, not irregularly. PR 195 ms, QRS 74 ms, QT ~320 ms giving QTc (Bazett) ~375 ms. Frontal QRS axis +46 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block and no AV block. This is the patient's only ECG, so there is no prior tracing for comparison. It confirms sinus rhythm as documented in the same-day 2026-03-07 clinic note.

Sinus rhythm at 104/min, regular, with a prominent P wave before every QRS; PR 150 ms, QRS 92 ms (no bundle branch block), QT ~335 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~442 ms, axis +38 degrees (normal). The prior ECG 100698634 (2025-06-20) showed sinus tachycardia at 147/min with PR 140 ms, QRS 84 ms and QTc ~485 ms; the rate has fallen substantially but the QTc change (~43 ms) is below the 60 ms threshold and there is no change in rhythm or conduction.

Sinus tachycardia at 108/min with P waves preceding each QRS, PR 130 ms, QRS 86 ms, QT ~325 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~438 ms, frontal axis +35 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block and no AV block. Single ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response: irregularly irregular RR intervals (173-359 samples, normalised RMSSD 0.22), no P waves identifiable on the signal-averaged beat, mean ventricular rate ~136/min, so no PR interval can be measured. QRS 84 ms with no bundle branch block; QT ~285 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~431 ms; axis +3 degrees (normal). The prior ECG 107914094, recorded 2 hours 23 minutes earlier the same day, also showed atrial fibrillation at ~133/min with QTc ~428 ms, so there is no change. Note that the clinic note of the same morning described 'normal sinus rhythm, rate 72', which these tracings contradict (separate contradiction item).

Sinus rhythm at 69/min, regular, P wave before every QRS, PR 165 ms, QRS 74 ms (no bundle branch block), QT ~405 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~432 ms. Frontal QRS axis about -25 degrees, within the normal range. The prior ECG 104232242 (2025-04-27) was sinus at ~61/min with PR 150 ms, QRS 74 ms and QTc ~404 ms; the frontal axis has shifted (previously markedly leftward/extreme), but rhythm, conduction and QTc are unchanged (QTc change ~28 ms).

Sinus rhythm at 98/min, regular, with P waves before each QRS; PR 116 ms, QRS 70 ms, QT ~310 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~393 ms, axis +4 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block, no AV block. Only ECG available, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 72/min, regular, with normal P waves; PR 146 ms, QRS 78 ms, QT ~380 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~417 ms, frontal axis +22 degrees (normal). No conduction abnormality. Only one ECG exists for this patient (2025-12-25), so no prior comparison; note that no ECG has been obtained since escitalopram was started on 2026-08-01 (separate follow-up item).

Atrial fibrillation: irregularly irregular RR intervals (347-583 samples, normalised RMSSD 0.30) with no organised P wave on the signal-averaged beat, mean ventricular rate ~61/min, so no PR interval is measurable. QRS 84 ms with no bundle branch block; QT ~455 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~457 ms; axis +27 degrees (normal). The prior ECG 107873952 (2024-11-12) showed regular sinus rhythm at 69/min with a clear P wave (PR ~190 ms) and QTc ~400 ms, so atrial fibrillation is new on this tracing (NEW_AF); the QTc change is below 60 ms. This corresponds to the atrial fibrillation coded at that admission, after which apixaban was started.

Sinus bradycardia at 58/min, essentially regular, with a P wave before every QRS; PR 110 ms, QRS 80 ms, QT ~420 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~412 ms, axis +62 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. The prior ECG 106045460 (2025-03-08, one day earlier) was also sinus at ~62/min with PR 112 ms, QRS 82 ms and QTc ~438 ms, so there are no changes (QTc change ~26 ms). No ECG has been obtained since haloperidol was started on 2026-09-15.

Sinus rhythm at 83/min, regular, with P waves before each QRS; PR 162 ms, QRS 66 ms, QT ~335 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~396 ms, axis +53 degrees (normal). No conduction abnormality. Single ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 76/min, regular, with clear P waves; PR 162 ms, QRS 66 ms, QT ~400 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~449 ms, frontal axis +65 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block and no AV block. The prior ECG 109048192 (2020-02-02) showed sinus rhythm at 75/min with a longer PR of about 250 ms (first-degree AV block) and a late low-amplitude T wave giving QTc ~506 ms; on the present tracing the PR has normalised and the QTc has fallen by ~57 ms, which is just short of the 60 ms threshold, so no QTc change is reported.

Sinus tachycardia at 121/min, regular (RR 249 +/- 4 samples), with a discrete P wave ending about 120 ms before the QRS; PR at the upper limit of normal, ~200 ms, so no first-degree AV block is called. QRS 86 ms with no bundle branch block; QT ~270 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~383 ms; axis +53 degrees (normal). Compared with the prior ECG 106186980 (2016-09-16, sinus at 108/min, PR ~185 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc ~394 ms) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc (change 11 ms).

Sinus bradycardia at 55/min, regular, with a P wave before every QRS but a prolonged PR interval of about 212 ms, i.e. first-degree AV block. QRS 80 ms with no bundle branch block; QT ~400 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~381 ms; frontal axis about +4 degrees (normal). The prior ECG 103042067 (2024-11-30) also showed sinus bradycardia (~51/min) with a prolonged PR (~200-215 ms) and QTc ~365 ms, so there is no new change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response: RR intervals are irregularly irregular (144-291 samples, normalised RMSSD 0.27) with no organised atrial activity on the signal-averaged beat; mean ventricular rate ~151/min and no measurable PR interval. QRS 70 ms with no bundle branch block; QT ~265 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~419 ms; axis about -13 degrees (normal). The prior ECG 107374881 (2025-09-12) showed sinus rhythm at ~77/min with a P wave and PR ~155 ms (a single premature beat accounting for the one short RR), and the tracing before that (102247352) was metronomically regular sinus rhythm; atrial fibrillation is therefore new (NEW_AF), matching the post-operative atrial fibrillation coded at this admission. QTc unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 72/min with a P wave before every QRS, PR 182 ms, QRS 84 ms, QT ~350 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~383 ms, axis +13 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. The prior ECG 105362569 (2025-11-21) was also sinus (67/min, PR 165 ms) but with a much longer QT, QTc ~528 ms; the QTc has therefore fallen by well over 60 ms (QTC_DECREASE_60). This tracing confirms the sinus rhythm documented in the same-day 2025-11-23 clinic note.

Sinus rhythm at 74/min, regular, with P waves before every QRS; PR 186 ms, QRS 82 ms, QT ~380 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~422 ms, axis +56 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block and no AV block. Single ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus tachycardia at 112/min. The rhythm is extremely regular (RR 268-270 samples) and a single discrete biphasic atrial deflection is seen once per cycle, beginning about 215 ms before each QRS with a flat isoelectric TP segment in between - one P per QRS, so this is sinus and not 2:1 atrial flutter despite the history of atrial flutter. PR ~185 ms, QRS 90 ms (no bundle branch block), QT ~290 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~395 ms, axis +35 degrees (normal). The prior ECG 102955795 (2022-07-04) was virtually identical (sinus 115/min, PR ~180 ms, QRS 88 ms, QTc ~384 ms), so there are no changes.

Sinus rhythm at 62/min. The baseline RR intervals are regular (478-493 samples) with a single premature beat (281 samples followed by a 683-sample pause), and a reproducible P wave is present about 200 ms before each QRS, so this is sinus rhythm with an isolated premature complex rather than atrial fibrillation. PR ~198 ms (upper normal), QRS 92 ms with no bundle branch block, QT ~370 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~378 ms. Frontal QRS axis about -32 degrees, i.e. left axis deviation. This is the only ECG for the patient, so no prior comparison; her paroxysmal atrial fibrillation is documented by diagnosis rather than by this tracing.

Sinus rhythm at 70/min, regular, with a P wave before every QRS; PR 144 ms, QRS 88 ms (no bundle branch block), QT ~355 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~383 ms. The frontal QRS axis is about -173 degrees - the QRS is predominantly negative in both I and aVF with a dominant positive complex in aVR - i.e. an extreme (north-west) axis; limb-lead reversal should be excluded clinically. Only one ECG exists for this patient, so no prior comparison. It was recorded 2026-04-29, outside the 14-day window after escitalopram was started on 2026-04-10 (separate follow-up item).

Sinus rhythm at 70/min, regular, with normal P waves; PR 166 ms, QRS 90 ms (no bundle branch block), axis +36 degrees (normal). Repolarisation is grossly prolonged with a broad late T wave: QT ~505 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~548 ms. The prior ECG 107149156 (2020-06-17) showed sinus tachycardia at 132/min with QTc ~416 ms, so the QTc has increased by far more than 60 ms. The patient takes citalopram 40 mg daily, so this exceeds the clinic's 500 ms review threshold (separate QT safety item).

Sinus rhythm at 68/min, regular, with a P wave (biphasic in V1) before every QRS; PR 164 ms, QRS 78 ms, axis +65 degrees (normal), no bundle branch block or AV block. The T wave is inverted in I, aVL and V2 with QT ~420 ms, giving QTc (Bazett) ~445 ms - below the 500 ms review threshold. This is the patient's only ECG, obtained 2026-03-08 within 30 days of the 2026-02-12 escitalopram start, so no prior comparison is possible.

Sinus bradycardia at 53/min, regular, with P waves before every QRS; PR 180 ms, QRS 84 ms, QT ~380 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~356 ms, frontal axis about -5 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. The prior ECG 108651109 (2018-12-13) was sinus at 66/min with a PR of about 210 ms and QTc ~385 ms; on the current tracing the PR is within normal limits and the QTc change (~29 ms) is below the 60 ms threshold, so no changes are reported.

Sinus rhythm at 68/min with normal P waves, PR 158 ms and QRS 84 ms, axis +46 degrees (normal), no bundle branch block. Repolarisation is markedly abnormal: a long isoelectric ST segment with a late broad T wave peaking ~365 ms after the R, giving QT ~490 ms and QTc (Bazett) ~520 ms. Compared with the prior ECG 100065910 (2022-11-23, sinus 75/min, QTc ~355 ms) the QTc has increased by well over 60 ms. The patient is on escitalopram, so this crosses the clinic's 500 ms review threshold (separate QT safety item).

Sinus tachycardia at 141/min. The rhythm is regular (RR 201-227 samples, normalised RMSSD 0.03) and a reproducible atrial deflection precedes each QRS by about 150-170 ms with only one atrial wave per ventricular cycle, so the rhythm is organised rather than fibrillating; the P axis is atypical (negative in I, positive in III), suggesting a low atrial/ectopic focus. PR ~148 ms, QRS 78 ms (no bundle branch block), QT ~265 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~404 ms, axis +1 degree (normal). The prior ECG 109839112 (2022-07-11) showed atrial fibrillation - irregularly irregular RR intervals (190-412 samples, RMSSD 0.33) with no P waves - so atrial fibrillation has resolved on this tracing (RESOLVED_AF). No pacing spikes are seen despite the coded pacemaker.

Sinus rhythm at 82/min, regular, with a P wave before every QRS; PR 186 ms, QRS 96 ms - slightly widened but below 120 ms, so no bundle branch block is diagnosed. QT ~370 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~436 ms; frontal axis +34 degrees (normal). Single ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 91/min, very regular, with a P wave beginning about 190 ms before each QRS (PR ~158 ms once the drifting TP baseline is accounted for). QRS 76 ms with no bundle branch block; QT ~335 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~414 ms; frontal axis about -19 degrees (normal). The prior ECG 102616671 (2021-05-16) was also sinus at 87/min with a similar PR, QRS 78 ms and QTc ~393 ms, so there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

Sinus rhythm at 59/min with a P wave before every QRS but a prolonged PR of about 208 ms (first-degree AV block). The QRS is wide at 126 ms with a broad monophasic R wave in I and aVL, deep wide negative complexes in V1-V4 and no septal q waves - a left bundle branch block pattern. QT ~445 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~440 ms; frontal axis about -21 degrees (normal range). The prior ECG 103686933 (2024-06-03) showed the same picture (sinus ~68/min, PR ~225 ms, QRS 126 ms with identical LBBB morphology, QTc ~453 ms), so the bundle branch block is not new and there are no changes.

Sinus rhythm at 102/min, regular, with P waves before every QRS; PR 148 ms, QRS 82 ms, QT ~330 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~427 ms, axis +46 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. The prior ECG 101016166 (2025-03-18, the previous day) was also sinus at 101/min with QRS 80 ms and QTc ~421 ms, so there are no changes.

Sinus rhythm at 66/min, regular, with a P wave before every QRS; PR 186 ms, QRS 84 ms, QT ~370 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~385 ms. Frontal QRS axis about -20 to -28 degrees, within the normal range. No bundle branch block and no AV block. This is the patient's only ECG, so no prior comparison is possible.

Sinus bradycardia at 58/min with a reproducible P wave about 195 ms before each QRS and only mild RR variability; QRS 84 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis +37 degrees (normal). Repolarisation is markedly prolonged with a very broad late T wave: QT ~550 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~542 ms. The prior ECG 100867733 (2022-04-06) showed atrial fibrillation at ~130/min (RR 162-308 samples, no P waves) with QTc ~453 ms. Compared with it, atrial fibrillation has resolved (RESOLVED_AF) and the QTc has increased by more than 60 ms (QTC_INCREASE_60) - relevant given continuing amiodarone (separate QT safety item).

Sinus tachycardia at 107/min, regular, with a P wave about 165 ms before each QRS (after allowing for the baseline drift between the TP and PR segments). QRS 66 ms with no bundle branch block; QT ~310-330 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~417 ms; frontal axis +53 degrees (normal). The prior ECG 107274479 (2019-07-27) was sinus at 75/min with PR ~160 ms, QRS 68 ms and QTc ~423 ms, so there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

Sinus tachycardia at 121/min, regular, with a P wave before each QRS; PR 148 ms, QRS 74 ms, QT ~285 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~406 ms. Frontal axis +68 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block and no AV block. Only one ECG exists for this patient, so no prior comparison is possible.

Sinus rhythm at 102/min (mild sinus tachycardia), regular, P wave before every QRS, PR 188 ms, QRS 82 ms, QT ~320 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~414 ms, axis +57 degrees (normal). No conduction block. The prior tracing 102910502 was recorded 34 seconds earlier the same day and is essentially identical (rate 100/min, PR 190 ms, QRS 84 ms, QTc ~408 ms), so there are no interval changes.

Sinus bradycardia at 52/min, regular (RR variation <1%), with low-amplitude but consistent P waves before each QRS; PR 175 ms, QRS 84 ms, QT ~430 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~399 ms, axis +36 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block; despite the historical coding of Mobitz II AV block there are no dropped beats or PR prolongation on this tracing. The prior ECG 104629882 (2023-05-22) was also sinus (~58/min) with a single premature beat and QTc ~391 ms, so there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

Sinus tachycardia at 122/min, very regular, P wave before every QRS, PR 142 ms. The QRS is now narrow at 84 ms with a rightward frontal axis of about +141 degrees; QT ~290 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~410 ms. The prior ECG 106516875, recorded only 13 hours earlier the same day, showed a QRS of ~146 ms with an rSR' configuration in V1 (terminal R' 1.1 mV) and wide terminal S waves in I and V6 - typical right bundle branch block, matching the patient's coded RBBB. The wide complex has resolved on this tracing, so RESOLVED_BUNDLE_BRANCH_BLOCK is reported; QTc changed by only ~55 ms (465 to 410 ms), below the 60 ms threshold.

Sinus rhythm at 62/min, regular, with P waves before every QRS, PR 180 ms, QRS 92 ms (no bundle branch block), axis +66 degrees (normal). Repolarisation is prolonged - a broad T wave ending about 470 ms after the QRS onset - giving QT ~515 ms and QTc (Bazett) ~531 ms. The prior ECG 108780865 (2025-06-07) was sinus at ~49/min with QTc ~414 ms, so QTc has increased by more than 60 ms, coinciding with amiodarone being started at the 2025-11-10 clinic visit.

Atrial fibrillation: the rhythm is irregularly irregular (RR intervals 193-548 samples, normalised RMSSD 0.42) with no organised P waves on the signal-averaged beat (residual atrial amplitude at noise level), mean ventricular rate ~100/min. No measurable PR interval. QRS 76 ms with no bundle branch block; QT ~315 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~409 ms. Frontal QRS axis about -51 degrees, i.e. left axis deviation. This is the only ECG for the patient, so no prior comparison is possible; it is consistent with his coded atrial fibrillation, for which he takes warfarin.

Outside-records summary of 2026-08-12 documents an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 to Mercy Hospital for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9, 2 units transfused) with apixaban held at discharge pending cardiology review. Two oral anticoagulants are current for this patient with paroxysmal/persistent atrial fibrillation. At the 2026-07-15 cardiology clinic visit the plan was to switch rivaroxaban to apixaban ('Switching anticoagulant from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage. Start apixaban 5 mg twice daily'), but rivaroxaban 20 mg daily was re-ordered the same day (valid 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-25) alongside the new apixaban 5 mg twice daily order (valid 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-26), and the note's own medication list shows both drugs. Rivaroxaban was never discontinued, so as of 2026-09-24 the patient has overlapping apixaban and rivaroxaban - a major bleeding hazard requiring immediate reconciliation.

The clinic note of 2026-06-10 10:55 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that same day contradict this: 107914094 (2026-06-10 17:13) shows an irregularly irregular rhythm at a mean ventricular rate of about 133/min with no discernible P waves, and 103088543 (2026-06-10 19:36) shows the same at about 136/min - i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, not sinus rhythm at 72. Unspecified atrial fibrillation was in fact coded at the 2026-06-10/12 encounter and warfarin was started. The documented rhythm and rate need correction and the rate-control/anticoagulation plan re-reviewed.

The baseline RR intervals are regular (478-493 samples) with a single premature beat (281 samples followed by a 683-sample pause), and a reproducible P wave is present about 200 ms before each QRS, so this is sinus rhythm with an isolated premature complex rather than atrial fibrillation. PR ~198 ms (upper normal), QRS 92 ms with no bundle branch block, QT ~370 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~378 ms. Frontal QRS axis about -32 degrees, i.e. left axis deviation. This is the only ECG for the patient, so no prior comparison; her paroxysmal atrial fibrillation is documented by diagnosis rather than by this tracing.

The clinic note of 2026-06-10 10:55 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Two oral anticoagulants are current for this patient with paroxysmal/persistent atrial fibrillation. At the 2026-07-15 cardiology clinic visit the plan was to switch rivaroxaban to apixaban ('Switching anticoagulant from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage. Rivaroxaban was never discontinued, so as of 2026-09-24 the patient has overlapping apixaban and rivaroxaban - a major bleeding hazard requiring immediate reconciliation.

The clinic note of 2026-06-10 10:55 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that same day contradict this: 107914094 (2026-06-10 17:13) shows an irregularly irregular rhythm at a mean ventricular rate of about 133/min with no discernible P waves, and 103088543 (2026-06-10 19:36) shows the same at about 136/min - i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, not sinus rhythm at 72. Unspecified atrial fibrillation was in fact coded at the 2026-06-10/12 encounter and warfarin was started. The documented rhythm and rate need correction and the rate-control/anticoagulation plan re-reviewed.

arguments.explanation: Sinus tachycardia at 141/min. The rhythm is regular (RR 201-227 samples, normalised RMSSD 0.03) and a reproducible atrial deflection precedes each QRS by about 150-170 ms with only one atrial wave per ventricular cycle, so the rhythm is organised rather than fibrillating; the P axis is atypical (negative in I, positive in III), suggesting a low atrial/ectopic focus. PR ~148 ms, QRS 78 ms (no bundle branch block), QT ~265 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~404 ms, axis +1 degree (normal). The prior ECG 109839112 (2022-07-11) showed atrial fibrillation - irregularly irregular RR intervals (190-412 samples, RMSSD 0.33) with no P waves - so atrial fibrillation has resolved on this tracing (RESOLVED_AF). No pacing spikes are seen despite the coded pacemaker.

Two oral anticoagulants are current for this patient with paroxysmal/persistent atrial fibrillation. The clinic note of 2026-06-10 10:55 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that same day contradict this: 107914094 (2026-06-10 17:13) shows an irregularly irregular rhythm at a mean ventricular rate of about 133/min with no discernible P waves, and 103088543 (2026-06-10 19:36) shows the same at about 136/min - i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, not sinus rhythm at 72. Unspecified atrial fibrillation was in fact coded at the 2026-06-10/12 encounter and warfarin was started. The documented rhythm and rate need correction and the rate-control/anticoagulation plan re-reviewed.

71-year-old woman (DOB 1955-09-07) with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (ICD-10 I48.0) documented during the 2025-03-14 admission for embolic cerebral infarction. Needs review for initiation of anticoagulation for secondary stroke prevention.

Outside-records summary of 2026-08-12 documents an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 to Mercy Hospital for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9, 2 units transfused) with apixaban held at discharge pending cardiology review. That review has not happened: at the 2026-08-20 clinic visit apixaban 5 mg twice daily was re-ordered (valid 2026-08-20 to 2026-12-28) and the note states 'continue current regimen', with concurrent aspirin 81 mg and clopidogrel 75 mg. A current anticoagulant (plus dual antiplatelet therapy) is therefore running despite a documented major GI bleed that was explicitly flagged as requiring review before resumption.

Two oral anticoagulants are current for this patient with paroxysmal/persistent atrial fibrillation. At the 2026-07-15 cardiology clinic visit the plan was to switch rivaroxaban to apixaban ('Switching anticoagulant from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage. Start apixaban 5 mg twice daily'), but rivaroxaban 20 mg daily was re-ordered the same day (valid 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-25) alongside the new apixaban 5 mg twice daily order (valid 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-26), and the note's own medication list shows both drugs. Rivaroxaban was never discontinued, so as of 2026-09-24 the patient has overlapping apixaban and rivaroxaban - a major bleeding hazard requiring immediate reconciliation.

The clinic note of 2026-06-10 10:55 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that same day contradict this: 107914094 (2026-06-10 17:13) shows an irregularly irregular rhythm at a mean ventricular rate of about 133/min with no discernible P waves, and 103088543 (2026-06-10 19:36) shows the same at about 136/min - i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, not sinus rhythm at 72. Unspecified atrial fibrillation was in fact coded at the 2026-06-10/12 encounter and warfarin was started. The documented rhythm and rate need correction and the rate-control/anticoagulation plan re-reviewed.

interpretations.explanation: Sinus rhythm at 81/min with a clear upright P wave in II/III/aVF (negative in aVL) preceding every QRS; RR intervals vary smoothly (329-429 samples) as respiratory sinus variation, not irregularly. PR 195 ms, QRS 74 ms, QT ~320 ms giving QTc (Bazett) ~375 ms. Frontal QRS axis +46 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block and no AV block. This is the patient's only ECG, so there is no prior tracing for comparison. It confirms sinus rhythm as documented in the same-day 2026-03-07 clinic note.

Sinus tachycardia at 121/min, regular (RR 249 +/- 4 samples), with a discrete P wave ending about 120 ms before the QRS; PR at the upper limit of normal, ~200 ms, so no first-degree AV block is called. QRS 86 ms with no bundle branch block; QT ~270 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~383 ms; axis +53 degrees (normal). Compared with the prior ECG 106186980 (2016-09-16, sinus at 108/min, PR ~185 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc ~394 ms) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc (change 11 ms).

arguments.explanation: Sinus rhythm at 68/min with normal P waves, PR 158 ms and QRS 84 ms, axis +46 degrees (normal), no bundle branch block. The patient is on escitalopram, so this crosses the clinic's 500 ms review threshold (separate QT safety item).

No anticoagulant is ordered - current medications per the 2026-07-10 clinic note are carvedilol, metoprolol tartrate and famotidine only, and no anticoagulant appears anywhere in the medication record. Needs review for initiation of anticoagulation for secondary stroke prevention.

A current anticoagulant (plus dual antiplatelet therapy) is therefore running despite a documented major GI bleed that was explicitly flagged as requiring review before resumption.

Two oral anticoagulants are current for this patient with paroxysmal/persistent atrial fibrillation. At the 2026-07-15 cardiology clinic visit the plan was to switch rivaroxaban to apixaban ('Switching anticoagulant from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage. Start apixaban 5 mg twice daily'), but rivaroxaban 20 mg daily was re-ordered the same day (valid 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-25) alongside the new apixaban 5 mg twice daily order (valid 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-26), and the note's own medication list shows both drugs. Rivaroxaban was never discontinued, so as of 2026-09-24 the patient has overlapping apixaban and rivaroxaban - a major bleeding hazard requiring immediate reconciliation.

The clinic note of 2026-06-10 10:55 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that same day contradict this: 107914094 (2026-06-10 17:13) shows an irregularly irregular rhythm at a mean ventricular rate of about 133/min with no discernible P waves, and 103088543 (2026-06-10 19:36) shows the same at about 136/min - i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, not sinus rhythm at 72. Unspecified atrial fibrillation was in fact coded at the 2026-06-10/12 encounter and warfarin was started. The documented rhythm and rate need correction and the rate-control/anticoagulation plan re-reviewed.

INR 2.3 was resulted on 2026-09-05 (Observation d6b3bad5), four days after the change, so the monitoring requirement was completed.

The most recent INR in the chart is 2.6 from 2026-08-22; no INR has been resulted since the dose change, so the requirement is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

71-year-old woman (DOB 1955-09-07) with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (ICD-10 I48.0) documented during the 2025-03-14 admission for embolic cerebral infarction. CHA2DS2-VASc 5: female sex 1, age 65-74 1, hypertension 1, prior stroke 2. Guideline recommends oral anticoagulation. No anticoagulant is ordered - current medications per the 2026-07-10 clinic note are carvedilol, metoprolol tartrate and famotidine only, and no anticoagulant appears anywhere in the medication record. Needs review for initiation of anticoagulation for secondary stroke prevention.

Outside-records summary of 2026-08-12 documents an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 to Mercy Hospital for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9, 2 units transfused) with apixaban held at discharge pending cardiology review. That review has not happened: at the 2026-08-20 clinic visit apixaban 5 mg twice daily was re-ordered (valid 2026-08-20 to 2026-12-28) and the note states 'continue current regimen', with concurrent aspirin 81 mg and clopidogrel 75 mg. A current anticoagulant (plus dual antiplatelet therapy) is therefore running despite a documented major GI bleed that was explicitly flagged as requiring review before resumption.

Two oral anticoagulants are current for this patient with paroxysmal/persistent atrial fibrillation. At the 2026-07-15 cardiology clinic visit the plan was to switch rivaroxaban to apixaban ('Switching anticoagulant from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage. Start apixaban 5 mg twice daily'), but rivaroxaban 20 mg daily was re-ordered the same day (valid 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-25) alongside the new apixaban 5 mg twice daily order (valid 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-26), and the note's own medication list shows both drugs. Rivaroxaban was never discontinued, so as of 2026-09-24 the patient has overlapping apixaban and rivaroxaban - a major bleeding hazard requiring immediate reconciliation.

The clinic note of 2026-06-10 10:55 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that same day contradict this: 107914094 (2026-06-10 17:13) shows an irregularly irregular rhythm at a mean ventricular rate of about 133/min with no discernible P waves, and 103088543 (2026-06-10 19:36) shows the same at about 136/min - i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, not sinus rhythm at 72. Unspecified atrial fibrillation was in fact coded at the 2026-06-10/12 encounter and warfarin was started. The documented rhythm and rate need correction and the rate-control/anticoagulation plan re-reviewed.

Prescriber review of escitalopram is required; potassium 4.1 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (2025-08-23) are normal, so a repeat ECG and drug review are indicated.

Prescriber review of citalopram dose and a repeat ECG are required.

Sinus rhythm at 83/min, regular, with P waves before each QRS; PR 162 ms, QRS 66 ms, QT ~335 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~396 ms, axis +53 degrees (normal). No conduction abnormality. Single ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 62/min. This is the only ECG for the patient, so no prior comparison; her paroxysmal atrial fibrillation is documented by diagnosis rather than by this tracing.

Sinus rhythm at 70/min, regular, with a P wave before every QRS; PR 144 ms, QRS 88 ms (no bundle branch block), QT ~355 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~383 ms. Only one ECG exists for this patient, so no prior comparison. It was recorded 2026-04-29, outside the 14-day window after escitalopram was started on 2026-04-10 (separate follow-up item).

Sinus rhythm at 70/min, regular, with normal P waves; PR 166 ms, QRS 90 ms (no bundle branch block), axis +36 degrees (normal). Sinus rhythm at 68/min, regular, with a P wave (biphasic in V1) before every QRS; PR 164 ms, QRS 78 ms, axis +65 degrees (normal), no bundle branch block or AV block. This is the patient's only ECG, obtained 2026-03-08 within 30 days of the 2026-02-12 escitalopram start, so no prior comparison is possible.

Sinus bradycardia at 53/min, regular, with P waves before every QRS; PR 180 ms, QRS 84 ms, QT ~380 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~356 ms, frontal axis about -5 degrees (normal). Sinus rhythm at 68/min with normal P waves, PR 158 ms and QRS 84 ms, axis +46 degrees (normal), no bundle branch block. Compared with the prior ECG 100065910 (2022-11-23, sinus 75/min, QTc ~355 ms) the QTc has increased by well over 60 ms. The patient is on escitalopram, so this crosses the clinic's 500 ms review threshold (separate QT safety item).

Sinus tachycardia at 121/min, regular, with a P wave before each QRS; PR 148 ms, QRS 74 ms, QT ~285 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~406 ms. Frontal axis +68 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block and no AV block. Only one ECG exists for this patient, so no prior comparison is possible.

Sinus rhythm at 102/min (mild sinus tachycardia), regular, P wave before every QRS, PR 188 ms, QRS 82 ms, QT ~320 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~414 ms, axis +57 degrees (normal). No conduction block. The prior tracing 102910502 was recorded 34 seconds earlier the same day and is essentially identical (rate 100/min, PR 190 ms, QRS 84 ms, QTc ~408 ms), so there are no interval changes.

Sinus bradycardia at 52/min, regular (RR variation <1%), with low-amplitude but consistent P waves before each QRS; PR 175 ms, QRS 84 ms, QT ~430 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~399 ms, axis +36 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block; despite the historical coding of Mobitz II AV block there are no dropped beats or PR prolongation on this tracing. The prior ECG 104629882 (2023-05-22) was also sinus (~58/min) with a single premature beat and QTc ~391 ms, so there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

Sinus tachycardia at 122/min, very regular, P wave before every QRS, PR 142 ms. The QRS is now narrow at 84 ms with a rightward frontal axis of about +141 degrees; QT ~290 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~410 ms. The prior ECG 106516875, recorded only 13 hours earlier the same day, showed a QRS of ~146 ms with an rSR' configuration in V1 (terminal R' 1.1 mV) and wide terminal S waves in I and V6 - typical right bundle branch block, matching the patient's coded RBBB. The wide complex has resolved on this tracing, so RESOLVED_BUNDLE_BRANCH_BLOCK is reported; QTc changed by only ~55 ms (465 to 410 ms), below the 60 ms threshold.

Sinus rhythm at 62/min, regular, with P waves before every QRS, PR 180 ms, QRS 92 ms (no bundle branch block), axis +66 degrees (normal). Repolarisation is prolonged - a broad T wave ending about 470 ms after the QRS onset - giving QT ~515 ms and QTc (Bazett) ~531 ms. The prior ECG 108780865 (2025-06-07) was sinus at ~49/min with QTc ~414 ms, so QTc has increased by more than 60 ms, coinciding with amiodarone being started at the 2025-11-10 clinic visit.

Atrial fibrillation: the rhythm is irregularly irregular (RR intervals 193-548 samples, normalised RMSSD 0.42) with no organised P waves on the signal-averaged beat (residual atrial amplitude at noise level), mean ventricular rate ~100/min. This is the only ECG for the patient, so no prior comparison is possible; it is consistent with his coded atrial fibrillation, for which he takes warfarin.

Sinus rhythm at 98/min, regular, with P waves before each QRS; PR 116 ms, QRS 70 ms, QT ~310 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~393 ms, axis +4 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block, no AV block. Only ECG available, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 72/min, regular, with normal P waves; PR 146 ms, QRS 78 ms, QT ~380 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~417 ms, frontal axis +22 degrees (normal). No conduction abnormality. Sinus rhythm at 62/min. PR ~198 ms (upper normal), QRS 92 ms with no bundle branch block, QT ~370 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~378 ms. Frontal QRS axis about -32 degrees, i.e. left axis deviation. This is the only ECG for the patient, so no prior comparison; her paroxysmal atrial fibrillation is documented by diagnosis rather than by this tracing.

Sinus rhythm at 70/min, regular, with a P wave before every QRS; PR 144 ms, QRS 88 ms (no bundle branch block), QT ~355 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~383 ms. Only one ECG exists for this patient, so no prior comparison. It was recorded 2026-04-29, outside the 14-day window after escitalopram was started on 2026-04-10 (separate follow-up item).

Sinus rhythm at 70/min, regular, with normal P waves; PR 166 ms, QRS 90 ms (no bundle branch block), axis +36 degrees (normal). The prior ECG 107149156 (2020-06-17) showed sinus tachycardia at 132/min with QTc ~416 ms, so the QTc has increased by far more than 60 ms. The patient takes citalopram 40 mg daily, so this exceeds the clinic's 500 ms review threshold (separate QT safety item).

Sinus rhythm at 68/min, regular, with a P wave (biphasic in V1) before every QRS; PR 164 ms, QRS 78 ms, axis +65 degrees (normal), no bundle branch block or AV block. This is the patient's only ECG, obtained 2026-03-08 within 30 days of the 2026-02-12 escitalopram start, so no prior comparison is possible.

Sinus bradycardia at 53/min, regular, with P waves before every QRS; PR 180 ms, QRS 84 ms, QT ~380 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~356 ms, frontal axis about -5 degrees (normal). The prior ECG 108651109 (2018-12-13) was sinus at 66/min with a PR of about 210 ms and QTc ~385 ms; on the current tracing the PR is within normal limits and the QTc change (~29 ms) is below the 60 ms threshold, so no changes are reported.

Sinus rhythm at 68/min with normal P waves, PR 158 ms and QRS 84 ms, axis +46 degrees (normal), no bundle branch block. Compared with the prior ECG 100065910 (2022-11-23, sinus 75/min, QTc ~355 ms) the QTc has increased by well over 60 ms. The patient is on escitalopram, so this crosses the clinic's 500 ms review threshold (separate QT safety item).

Sinus tachycardia at 141/min. The rhythm is regular (RR 201-227 samples, normalised RMSSD 0.03) and a reproducible atrial deflection precedes each QRS by about 150-170 ms with only one atrial wave per ventricular cycle, so the rhythm is organised rather than fibrillating; the P axis is atypical (negative in I, positive in III), suggesting a low atrial/ectopic focus. PR ~148 ms, QRS 78 ms (no bundle branch block), QT ~265 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~404 ms, axis +1 degree (normal). The prior ECG 109839112 (2022-07-11) showed atrial fibrillation - irregularly irregular RR intervals (190-412 samples, RMSSD 0.33) with no P waves - so atrial fibrillation has resolved on this tracing (RESOLVED_AF). No pacing spikes are seen despite the coded pacemaker.

Sinus tachycardia at 121/min, regular, with a P wave before each QRS; PR 148 ms, QRS 74 ms, QT ~285 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~406 ms. Frontal axis +68 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block and no AV block. Only one ECG exists for this patient, so no prior comparison is possible.

Sinus rhythm at 102/min (mild sinus tachycardia), regular, P wave before every QRS, PR 188 ms, QRS 82 ms, QT ~320 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~414 ms, axis +57 degrees (normal). No conduction block. The prior tracing 102910502 was recorded 34 seconds earlier the same day and is essentially identical (rate 100/min, PR 190 ms, QRS 84 ms, QTc ~408 ms), so there are no interval changes.

Sinus bradycardia at 52/min, regular (RR variation <1%), with low-amplitude but consistent P waves before each QRS; PR 175 ms, QRS 84 ms, QT ~430 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~399 ms, axis +36 degrees (normal). The prior ECG 104629882 (2023-05-22) was also sinus (~58/min) with a single premature beat and QTc ~391 ms, so there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

Sinus tachycardia at 122/min, very regular, P wave before every QRS, PR 142 ms. The QRS is now narrow at 84 ms with a rightward frontal axis of about +141 degrees; QT ~290 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~410 ms. The wide complex has resolved on this tracing, so RESOLVED_BUNDLE_BRANCH_BLOCK is reported; QTc changed by only ~55 ms (465 to 410 ms), below the 60 ms threshold.

Sinus rhythm at 62/min, regular, with P waves before every QRS, PR 180 ms, QRS 92 ms (no bundle branch block), axis +66 degrees (normal). The prior ECG 108780865 (2025-06-07) was sinus at ~49/min with QTc ~414 ms, so QTc has increased by more than 60 ms, coinciding with amiodarone being started at the 2025-11-10 clinic visit.

Atrial fibrillation: the rhythm is irregularly irregular (RR intervals 193-548 samples, normalised RMSSD 0.42) with no organised P waves on the signal-averaged beat (residual atrial amplitude at noise level), mean ventricular rate ~100/min. This is the only ECG for the patient, so no prior comparison is possible; it is consistent with his coded atrial fibrillation, for which he takes warfarin.

items.explanation: 71-year-old man (DOB 1955-08-23) with atrial fibrillation documented 2025-08-22 (ICD-9 427.31) and carried in every cardiology clinic note through 2026-07-28. CHA2DS2-VASc 3 (age 65-74 = 1, hypertension = 1, vascular disease/coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery = 1); guideline recommends oral anticoagulation at score >=2 in men. No anticoagulant has ever been ordered - the only current medication is tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily. Needs review for initiation of anticoagulation.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2025-11-10 (first appearance in the note medication list). The 9/1/2025 memo applies because the start was before 3/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 30 days, i.e. by 2025-12-10. ECG 106885519 was recorded on 2025-11-24, 14 days after the start, so the requirement was met. (The ECG showed QTc about 531 ms - see the separate QT safety item.)

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-02-12. The start predates 3/1/2026, so the 9/1/2025 memo's 30-day window applies: ECG due by 2026-03-14. ECG 101538691 was obtained on 2026-03-08, within 30 days, so the requirement was completed. That ECG showed sinus rhythm at 68/min with QTc about 445 ms (below the 500 ms review threshold).

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-03-02. Because the start is on/after 3/1/2026 the revised memo applies and an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-03-16. ECG 104882441 was recorded on 2026-03-07, five days after the start, so the requirement was completed; it showed sinus rhythm at 81/min with QTc about 375 ms.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-04-10. Under the revised 3/1/2026 memo an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-04-24. No ECG was performed in that window; the only ECG in the chart, 107859369, was recorded on 2026-04-29 - 19 days after the start and five days after the deadline - so the requirement was not met within the required time and is overdue as of the 2026-09-24 evaluation.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started as an outpatient at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-01 (it was absent from the medication list at the 2026-06-24 visit and appears for the first time on 2026-08-01). Under the revised 3/1/2026 memo an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-08-15. No ECG has been obtained since 2025-12-25 (106035722), so the requirement is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-10, so under the revised 3/1/2026 memo an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-08-24. No ECG exists in the chart for this patient. However the nurse telephone note of 2026-08-25 (DocumentReference/5e12a8aa-0439-53cd-a194-cc1a277d296d) records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 8/18 - inside the required window - and that the report was requested by fax but not yet received. That outside tracing could satisfy the requirement, so the status cannot be determined until the report is obtained.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-15; it is new to the medication list at that visit. Under the revised 3/1/2026 memo an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-09-29. No ECG has been done since 2025-03-09 (104253928). As of the 2026-09-24 evaluation the requirement is not yet due, but the ECG must be obtained in the next five days.

At the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-01 Dr Paul Kessler documented 'INR today 1.6, subtherapeutic. Increase warfarin to 7.5 mg daily; recheck INR' - a warfarin dose change made by a clinic clinician after the 3/1/2026 effective date, so an INR was required within 7 days (by 2026-09-08). INR 2.3 was resulted on 2026-09-05 (Observation d6b3bad5), four days after the change, so the monitoring requirement was completed.

Anticoagulation clinic telephone note of 2026-09-10 by L. Nguyen, PharmD: 'Home INR 3.4. Warfarin decreased from 5 mg to 4 mg daily per protocol.' A clinic pharmacist is authorised to adjust warfarin under the 6/1/2024 standing order, so this is a qualifying dose change and an INR was required within 7 days, by 2026-09-17. The most recent INR in the chart is 2.6 from 2026-08-22; no INR has been resulted since the dose change, so the requirement is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

71-year-old woman (DOB 1955-09-07) with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (ICD-10 I48.0) documented during the 2025-03-14 admission for embolic cerebral infarction. CHA2DS2-VASc 5: female sex 1, age 65-74 1, hypertension 1, prior stroke 2. Guideline recommends oral anticoagulation. No anticoagulant is ordered - current medications per the 2026-07-10 clinic note are carvedilol, metoprolol tartrate and famotidine only, and no anticoagulant appears anywhere in the medication record. Needs review for initiation of anticoagulation for secondary stroke prevention.

Outside-records summary of 2026-08-12 documents an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 to Mercy Hospital for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9, 2 units transfused) with apixaban held at discharge pending cardiology review. That review has not happened: at the 2026-08-20 clinic visit apixaban 5 mg twice daily was re-ordered (valid 2026-08-20 to 2026-12-28) and the note states 'continue current regimen', with concurrent aspirin 81 mg and clopidogrel 75 mg. A current anticoagulant (plus dual antiplatelet therapy) is therefore running despite a documented major GI bleed that was explicitly flagged as requiring review before resumption.

Two oral anticoagulants are current for this patient with paroxysmal/persistent atrial fibrillation. At the 2026-07-15 cardiology clinic visit the plan was to switch rivaroxaban to apixaban ('Switching anticoagulant from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage. Start apixaban 5 mg twice daily'), but rivaroxaban 20 mg daily was re-ordered the same day (valid 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-25) alongside the new apixaban 5 mg twice daily order (valid 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-26), and the note's own medication list shows both drugs. Rivaroxaban was never discontinued, so as of 2026-09-24 the patient has overlapping apixaban and rivaroxaban - a major bleeding hazard requiring immediate reconciliation.

The clinic note of 2026-06-10 10:55 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that same day contradict this: 107914094 (2026-06-10 17:13) shows an irregularly irregular rhythm at a mean ventricular rate of about 133/min with no discernible P waves, and 103088543 (2026-06-10 19:36) shows the same at about 136/min - i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, not sinus rhythm at 72. Unspecified atrial fibrillation was in fact coded at the 2026-06-10/12 encounter and warfarin was started. The documented rhythm and rate need correction and the rate-control/anticoagulation plan re-reviewed.

Patient is on escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug per the 1/15/2025 QT monitoring memo), most recently re-ordered 2026-04-23 and current. His most recent ECG, 108018814 of 2023-10-08, shows sinus rhythm at 68/min with QT about 490 ms and a Bazett-corrected QTc of about 520 ms (>=500 ms), driven by a markedly prolonged ST segment and late broad T wave. Notably the 2024-05-14 note that started escitalopram described this same ECG as 'QT acceptable'. Prescriber review of escitalopram is required; potassium 4.1 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (2025-08-23) are normal, so a repeat ECG and drug review are indicated.

Patient is on citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch-list drug), current order 2026-05-29 to 2026-12-25. Her most recent ECG, 104821039 of 2023-11-10, shows sinus rhythm at 70/min with QT about 505 ms and QTc (Bazett) about 548 ms, well above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT monitoring memo; QTc had risen from 416 ms on the previous ECG (107149156, 2020-06-17). Citalopram at 40 mg is above the dose recommended when QT prolongation is a concern. Potassium 4.5 mEq/L (2026-01-21) and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (2023-12-01) are normal. Prescriber review of citalopram dose and a repeat ECG are required.

Patient with atrial fibrillation is on amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list drug), current order 2026-07-29 to 2027-01-05. His most recent ECG, 106885519 of 2025-11-24, shows sinus rhythm at 62/min with QT about 515 ms and QTc (Bazett) about 531 ms, i.e. >=500 ms; QTc rose from 414 ms on the preceding ECG (108780865, 2025-06-07) after amiodarone was started at the 2025-11-10 clinic visit. Potassium 4.4 mEq/L and magnesium 2.2 mg/dL (2026-04-20) are normal. Prescriber review of amiodarone is required per the clinic QT monitoring memo.

95-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation/flutter on amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list drug), current order 2026-08-22 to 2027-01-05, together with warfarin and metoprolol. Her most recent ECG, 101515306 of 2022-04-27, shows sinus rhythm at 58/min with QT about 550 ms and QTc (Bazett) about 542 ms, i.e. >=500 ms (QTc was 453 ms on the preceding ECG 100867733 three weeks earlier, when she was in atrial fibrillation). Magnesium is low-normal at 1.8 mg/dL with potassium 4.1 mEq/L (2026-02-14). No ECG has been obtained since 2022 despite continuous amiodarone; prescriber review and a current ECG are required.

interpretations.explanation: Sinus rhythm at 81/min with a clear upright P wave in II/III/aVF (negative in aVL) preceding every QRS; RR intervals vary smoothly (329-429 samples) as respiratory sinus variation, not irregularly. PR 195 ms, QRS 74 ms, QT ~320 ms giving QTc (Bazett) ~375 ms. Frontal QRS axis +46 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block and no AV block. This is the patient's only ECG, so there is no prior tracing for comparison. It confirms sinus rhythm as documented in the same-day 2026-03-07 clinic note.

Sinus rhythm at 104/min, regular, with a prominent P wave before every QRS; PR 150 ms, QRS 92 ms (no bundle branch block), QT ~335 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~442 ms, axis +38 degrees (normal). The prior ECG 100698634 (2025-06-20) showed sinus tachycardia at 147/min with PR 140 ms, QRS 84 ms and QTc ~485 ms; the rate has fallen substantially but the QTc change (~43 ms) is below the 60 ms threshold and there is no change in rhythm or conduction.

Sinus tachycardia at 108/min with P waves preceding each QRS, PR 130 ms, QRS 86 ms, QT ~325 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~438 ms, frontal axis +35 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block and no AV block. Single ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response: irregularly irregular RR intervals (173-359 samples, normalised RMSSD 0.22), no P waves identifiable on the signal-averaged beat, mean ventricular rate ~136/min, so no PR interval can be measured. QRS 84 ms with no bundle branch block; QT ~285 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~431 ms; axis +3 degrees (normal). The prior ECG 107914094, recorded 2 hours 23 minutes earlier the same day, also showed atrial fibrillation at ~133/min with QTc ~428 ms, so there is no change. Note that the clinic note of the same morning described 'normal sinus rhythm, rate 72', which these tracings contradict (separate contradiction item).

Sinus rhythm at 69/min, regular, P wave before every QRS, PR 165 ms, QRS 74 ms (no bundle branch block), QT ~405 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~432 ms. Frontal QRS axis about -25 degrees, within the normal range. The prior ECG 104232242 (2025-04-27) was sinus at ~61/min with PR 150 ms, QRS 74 ms and QTc ~404 ms; the frontal axis has shifted (previously markedly leftward/extreme), but rhythm, conduction and QTc are unchanged (QTc change ~28 ms).

Sinus rhythm at 98/min, regular, with P waves before each QRS; PR 116 ms, QRS 70 ms, QT ~310 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~393 ms, axis +4 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block, no AV block. Only ECG available, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 72/min, regular, with normal P waves; PR 146 ms, QRS 78 ms, QT ~380 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~417 ms, frontal axis +22 degrees (normal). No conduction abnormality. Only one ECG exists for this patient (2025-12-25), so no prior comparison; note that no ECG has been obtained since escitalopram was started on 2026-08-01 (separate follow-up item).

Atrial fibrillation: irregularly irregular RR intervals (347-583 samples, normalised RMSSD 0.30) with no organised P wave on the signal-averaged beat, mean ventricular rate ~61/min, so no PR interval is measurable. QRS 84 ms with no bundle branch block; QT ~455 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~457 ms; axis +27 degrees (normal). The prior ECG 107873952 (2024-11-12) showed regular sinus rhythm at 69/min with a clear P wave (PR ~190 ms) and QTc ~400 ms, so atrial fibrillation is new on this tracing (NEW_AF); the QTc change is below 60 ms. This corresponds to the atrial fibrillation coded at that admission, after which apixaban was started.

Sinus bradycardia at 58/min, essentially regular, with a P wave before every QRS; PR 110 ms, QRS 80 ms, QT ~420 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~412 ms, axis +62 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. The prior ECG 106045460 (2025-03-08, one day earlier) was also sinus at ~62/min with PR 112 ms, QRS 82 ms and QTc ~438 ms, so there are no changes (QTc change ~26 ms). No ECG has been obtained since haloperidol was started on 2026-09-15.

Sinus rhythm at 83/min, regular, with P waves before each QRS; PR 162 ms, QRS 66 ms, QT ~335 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~396 ms, axis +53 degrees (normal). No conduction abnormality. Single ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 76/min, regular, with clear P waves; PR 162 ms, QRS 66 ms, QT ~400 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~449 ms, frontal axis +65 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block and no AV block. The prior ECG 109048192 (2020-02-02) showed sinus rhythm at 75/min with a longer PR of about 250 ms (first-degree AV block) and a late low-amplitude T wave giving QTc ~506 ms; on the present tracing the PR has normalised and the QTc has fallen by ~57 ms, which is just short of the 60 ms threshold, so no QTc change is reported.

Sinus tachycardia at 121/min, regular (RR 249 +/- 4 samples), with a discrete P wave ending about 120 ms before the QRS; PR at the upper limit of normal, ~200 ms, so no first-degree AV block is called. QRS 86 ms with no bundle branch block; QT ~270 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~383 ms; axis +53 degrees (normal). Compared with the prior ECG 106186980 (2016-09-16, sinus at 108/min, PR ~185 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc ~394 ms) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc (change 11 ms).

Sinus bradycardia at 55/min, regular, with a P wave before every QRS but a prolonged PR interval of about 212 ms, i.e. first-degree AV block. QRS 80 ms with no bundle branch block; QT ~400 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~381 ms; frontal axis about +4 degrees (normal). The prior ECG 103042067 (2024-11-30) also showed sinus bradycardia (~51/min) with a prolonged PR (~200-215 ms) and QTc ~365 ms, so there is no new change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response: RR intervals are irregularly irregular (144-291 samples, normalised RMSSD 0.27) with no organised atrial activity on the signal-averaged beat; mean ventricular rate ~151/min and no measurable PR interval. QRS 70 ms with no bundle branch block; QT ~265 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~419 ms; axis about -13 degrees (normal). The prior ECG 107374881 (2025-09-12) showed sinus rhythm at ~77/min with a P wave and PR ~155 ms (a single premature beat accounting for the one short RR), and the tracing before that (102247352) was metronomically regular sinus rhythm; atrial fibrillation is therefore new (NEW_AF), matching the post-operative atrial fibrillation coded at this admission. QTc unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 72/min with a P wave before every QRS, PR 182 ms, QRS 84 ms, QT ~350 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~383 ms, axis +13 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. The prior ECG 105362569 (2025-11-21) was also sinus (67/min, PR 165 ms) but with a much longer QT, QTc ~528 ms; the QTc has therefore fallen by well over 60 ms (QTC_DECREASE_60). This tracing confirms the sinus rhythm documented in the same-day 2025-11-23 clinic note.

Sinus rhythm at 74/min, regular, with P waves before every QRS; PR 186 ms, QRS 82 ms, QT ~380 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~422 ms, axis +56 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block and no AV block. Single ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus tachycardia at 112/min. The rhythm is extremely regular (RR 268-270 samples) and a single discrete biphasic atrial deflection is seen once per cycle, beginning about 215 ms before each QRS with a flat isoelectric TP segment in between - one P per QRS, so this is sinus and not 2:1 atrial flutter despite the history of atrial flutter. PR ~185 ms, QRS 90 ms (no bundle branch block), QT ~290 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~395 ms, axis +35 degrees (normal). The prior ECG 102955795 (2022-07-04) was virtually identical (sinus 115/min, PR ~180 ms, QRS 88 ms, QTc ~384 ms), so there are no changes.

Sinus rhythm at 62/min. The baseline RR intervals are regular (478-493 samples) with a single premature beat (281 samples followed by a 683-sample pause), and a reproducible P wave is present about 200 ms before each QRS, so this is sinus rhythm with an isolated premature complex rather than atrial fibrillation. PR ~198 ms (upper normal), QRS 92 ms with no bundle branch block, QT ~370 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~378 ms. Frontal QRS axis about -32 degrees, i.e. left axis deviation. This is the only ECG for the patient, so no prior comparison; her paroxysmal atrial fibrillation is documented by diagnosis rather than by this tracing.

Sinus rhythm at 70/min, regular, with a P wave before every QRS; PR 144 ms, QRS 88 ms (no bundle branch block), QT ~355 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~383 ms. The frontal QRS axis is about -173 degrees - the QRS is predominantly negative in both I and aVF with a dominant positive complex in aVR - i.e. an extreme (north-west) axis; limb-lead reversal should be excluded clinically. Only one ECG exists for this patient, so no prior comparison. It was recorded 2026-04-29, outside the 14-day window after escitalopram was started on 2026-04-10 (separate follow-up item).

Sinus rhythm at 70/min, regular, with normal P waves; PR 166 ms, QRS 90 ms (no bundle branch block), axis +36 degrees (normal). Repolarisation is grossly prolonged with a broad late T wave: QT ~505 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~548 ms. The prior ECG 107149156 (2020-06-17) showed sinus tachycardia at 132/min with QTc ~416 ms, so the QTc has increased by far more than 60 ms. The patient takes citalopram 40 mg daily, so this exceeds the clinic's 500 ms review threshold (separate QT safety item).

Sinus rhythm at 68/min, regular, with a P wave (biphasic in V1) before every QRS; PR 164 ms, QRS 78 ms, axis +65 degrees (normal), no bundle branch block or AV block. The T wave is inverted in I, aVL and V2 with QT ~420 ms, giving QTc (Bazett) ~445 ms - below the 500 ms review threshold. This is the patient's only ECG, obtained 2026-03-08 within 30 days of the 2026-02-12 escitalopram start, so no prior comparison is possible.

Sinus bradycardia at 53/min, regular, with P waves before every QRS; PR 180 ms, QRS 84 ms, QT ~380 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~356 ms, frontal axis about -5 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. The prior ECG 108651109 (2018-12-13) was sinus at 66/min with a PR of about 210 ms and QTc ~385 ms; on the current tracing the PR is within normal limits and the QTc change (~29 ms) is below the 60 ms threshold, so no changes are reported.

Sinus rhythm at 68/min with normal P waves, PR 158 ms and QRS 84 ms, axis +46 degrees (normal), no bundle branch block. Repolarisation is markedly abnormal: a long isoelectric ST segment with a late broad T wave peaking ~365 ms after the R, giving QT ~490 ms and QTc (Bazett) ~520 ms. Compared with the prior ECG 100065910 (2022-11-23, sinus 75/min, QTc ~355 ms) the QTc has increased by well over 60 ms. The patient is on escitalopram, so this crosses the clinic's 500 ms review threshold (separate QT safety item).

Sinus tachycardia at 141/min. The rhythm is regular (RR 201-227 samples, normalised RMSSD 0.03) and a reproducible atrial deflection precedes each QRS by about 150-170 ms with only one atrial wave per ventricular cycle, so the rhythm is organised rather than fibrillating; the P axis is atypical (negative in I, positive in III), suggesting a low atrial/ectopic focus. PR ~148 ms, QRS 78 ms (no bundle branch block), QT ~265 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~404 ms, axis +1 degree (normal). The prior ECG 109839112 (2022-07-11) showed atrial fibrillation - irregularly irregular RR intervals (190-412 samples, RMSSD 0.33) with no P waves - so atrial fibrillation has resolved on this tracing (RESOLVED_AF). No pacing spikes are seen despite the coded pacemaker.

Sinus rhythm at 82/min, regular, with a P wave before every QRS; PR 186 ms, QRS 96 ms - slightly widened but below 120 ms, so no bundle branch block is diagnosed. QT ~370 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~436 ms; frontal axis +34 degrees (normal). Single ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 91/min, very regular, with a P wave beginning about 190 ms before each QRS (PR ~158 ms once the drifting TP baseline is accounted for). QRS 76 ms with no bundle branch block; QT ~335 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~414 ms; frontal axis about -19 degrees (normal). The prior ECG 102616671 (2021-05-16) was also sinus at 87/min with a similar PR, QRS 78 ms and QTc ~393 ms, so there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

Sinus rhythm at 59/min with a P wave before every QRS but a prolonged PR of about 208 ms (first-degree AV block). The QRS is wide at 126 ms with a broad monophasic R wave in I and aVL, deep wide negative complexes in V1-V4 and no septal q waves - a left bundle branch block pattern. QT ~445 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~440 ms; frontal axis about -21 degrees (normal range). The prior ECG 103686933 (2024-06-03) showed the same picture (sinus ~68/min, PR ~225 ms, QRS 126 ms with identical LBBB morphology, QTc ~453 ms), so the bundle branch block is not new and there are no changes.

Sinus tachycardia at 121/min, regular, with a P wave before each QRS; PR 148 ms, QRS 74 ms, QT ~285 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~406 ms. Frontal axis +68 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block and no AV block. Only one ECG exists for this patient, so no prior comparison is possible.

Sinus rhythm at 102/min (mild sinus tachycardia), regular, P wave before every QRS, PR 188 ms, QRS 82 ms, QT ~320 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~414 ms, axis +57 degrees (normal). No conduction block. The prior tracing 102910502 was recorded 34 seconds earlier the same day and is essentially identical (rate 100/min, PR 190 ms, QRS 84 ms, QTc ~408 ms), so there are no interval changes.

Sinus bradycardia at 52/min, regular (RR variation <1%), with low-amplitude but consistent P waves before each QRS; PR 175 ms, QRS 84 ms, QT ~430 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~399 ms, axis +36 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block; despite the historical coding of Mobitz II AV block there are no dropped beats or PR prolongation on this tracing. The prior ECG 104629882 (2023-05-22) was also sinus (~58/min) with a single premature beat and QTc ~391 ms, so there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

Sinus tachycardia at 122/min, very regular, P wave before every QRS, PR 142 ms. The QRS is now narrow at 84 ms with a rightward frontal axis of about +141 degrees; QT ~290 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~410 ms. The prior ECG 106516875, recorded only 13 hours earlier the same day, showed a QRS of ~146 ms with an rSR' configuration in V1 (terminal R' 1.1 mV) and wide terminal S waves in I and V6 - typical right bundle branch block, matching the patient's coded RBBB. The wide complex has resolved on this tracing, so RESOLVED_BUNDLE_BRANCH_BLOCK is reported; QTc changed by only ~55 ms (465 to 410 ms), below the 60 ms threshold.

Sinus rhythm at 62/min, regular, with P waves before every QRS, PR 180 ms, QRS 92 ms (no bundle branch block), axis +66 degrees (normal). Repolarisation is prolonged - a broad T wave ending about 470 ms after the QRS onset - giving QT ~515 ms and QTc (Bazett) ~531 ms. The prior ECG 108780865 (2025-06-07) was sinus at ~49/min with QTc ~414 ms, so QTc has increased by more than 60 ms, coinciding with amiodarone being started at the 2025-11-10 clinic visit.

Atrial fibrillation: the rhythm is irregularly irregular (RR intervals 193-548 samples, normalised RMSSD 0.42) with no organised P waves on the signal-averaged beat (residual atrial amplitude at noise level), mean ventricular rate ~100/min. No measurable PR interval. QRS 76 ms with no bundle branch block; QT ~315 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~409 ms. Frontal QRS axis about -51 degrees, i.e. left axis deviation. This is the only ECG for the patient, so no prior comparison is possible; it is consistent with his coded atrial fibrillation, for which he takes warfarin.

Only one ECG exists for this patient, so no prior comparison. It was recorded 2026-04-29, outside the 14-day window after escitalopram was started on 2026-04-10 (separate follow-up item).

PR 195 ms, QRS 74 ms, QT ~320 ms giving QTc (Bazett) ~375 ms. Frontal QRS axis +46 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block and no AV block. This is the patient's only ECG, so there is no prior tracing for comparison. It confirms sinus rhythm as documented in the same-day 2026-03-07 clinic note.

Sinus rhythm at 104/min, regular, with a prominent P wave before every QRS; PR 150 ms, QRS 92 ms (no bundle branch block), QT ~335 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~442 ms, axis +38 degrees (normal). The prior ECG 100698634 (2025-06-20) showed sinus tachycardia at 147/min with PR 140 ms, QRS 84 ms and QTc ~485 ms; the rate has fallen substantially but the QTc change (~43 ms) is below the 60 ms threshold and there is no change in rhythm or conduction.

Sinus tachycardia at 108/min with P waves preceding each QRS, PR 130 ms, QRS 86 ms, QT ~325 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~438 ms, frontal axis +35 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block and no AV block. Single ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response: irregularly irregular RR intervals (173-359 samples, normalised RMSSD 0.22), no P waves identifiable on the signal-averaged beat, mean ventricular rate ~136/min, so no PR interval can be measured. QRS 84 ms with no bundle branch block; QT ~285 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~431 ms; axis +3 degrees (normal). Sinus rhythm at 69/min, regular, P wave before every QRS, PR 165 ms, QRS 74 ms (no bundle branch block), QT ~405 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~432 ms. Frontal QRS axis about -25 degrees, within the normal range. Sinus rhythm at 98/min, regular, with P waves before each QRS; PR 116 ms, QRS 70 ms, QT ~310 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~393 ms, axis +4 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block, no AV block. Only ECG available, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 72/min, regular, with normal P waves; PR 146 ms, QRS 78 ms, QT ~380 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~417 ms, frontal axis +22 degrees (normal). No conduction abnormality. Sinus rhythm at 72/min with a P wave before every QRS, PR 182 ms, QRS 84 ms, QT ~350 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~383 ms, axis +13 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. Sinus rhythm at 74/min, regular, with P waves before every QRS; PR 186 ms, QRS 82 ms, QT ~380 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~422 ms, axis +56 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block and no AV block. Single ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus tachycardia at 112/min. The rhythm is extremely regular (RR 268-270 samples) and a single discrete biphasic atrial deflection is seen once per cycle, beginning about 215 ms before each QRS with a flat isoelectric TP segment in between - one P per QRS, so this is sinus and not 2:1 atrial flutter despite the history of atrial flutter. PR ~185 ms, QRS 90 ms (no bundle branch block), QT ~290 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~395 ms, axis +35 degrees (normal). The prior ECG 102955795 (2022-07-04) was virtually identical (sinus 115/min, PR ~180 ms, QRS 88 ms, QTc ~384 ms), so there are no changes.

Sinus rhythm at 62/min. The baseline RR intervals are regular (478-493 samples) with a single premature beat (281 samples followed by a 683-sample pause), and a reproducible P wave is present about 200 ms before each QRS, so this is sinus rhythm with an isolated premature complex rather than atrial fibrillation. PR ~198 ms (upper normal), QRS 92 ms with no bundle branch block, QT ~370 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~378 ms. Frontal QRS axis about -32 degrees, i.e. left axis deviation. This is the only ECG for the patient, so no prior comparison; her paroxysmal atrial fibrillation is documented by diagnosis rather than by this tracing.

Sinus rhythm at 70/min, regular, with a P wave before every QRS; PR 144 ms, QRS 88 ms (no bundle branch block), QT ~355 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~383 ms. The frontal QRS axis is about -173 degrees - the QRS is predominantly negative in both I and aVF with a dominant positive complex in aVR - i.e. an extreme (north-west) axis; limb-lead reversal should be excluded clinically. Only one ECG exists for this patient, so no prior comparison. It was recorded 2026-04-29, outside the 14-day window after escitalopram was started on 2026-04-10 (separate follow-up item).

Sinus rhythm at 70/min, regular, with normal P waves; PR 166 ms, QRS 90 ms (no bundle branch block), axis +36 degrees (normal). Sinus rhythm at 68/min, regular, with a P wave (biphasic in V1) before every QRS; PR 164 ms, QRS 78 ms, axis +65 degrees (normal), no bundle branch block or AV block. Sinus rhythm at 66/min, regular, with a P wave before every QRS; PR 186 ms, QRS 84 ms, QT ~370 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~385 ms. Frontal QRS axis about -20 to -28 degrees, within the normal range. No bundle branch block and no AV block. This is the patient's only ECG, so no prior comparison is possible.

Sinus tachycardia at 121/min, regular, with a P wave before each QRS; PR 148 ms, QRS 74 ms, QT ~285 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~406 ms. Frontal axis +68 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block and no AV block. Only one ECG exists for this patient, so no prior comparison is possible.

The wide complex has resolved on this tracing, so RESOLVED_BUNDLE_BRANCH_BLOCK is reported; QTc changed by only ~55 ms (465 to 410 ms), below the 60 ms threshold.

Sinus rhythm at 62/min, regular, with P waves before every QRS, PR 180 ms, QRS 92 ms (no bundle branch block), axis +66 degrees (normal). Atrial fibrillation: the rhythm is irregularly irregular (RR intervals 193-548 samples, normalised RMSSD 0.42) with no organised P waves on the signal-averaged beat (residual atrial amplitude at noise level), mean ventricular rate ~100/min. 71-year-old woman (DOB 1955-09-07) with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (ICD-10 I48.0) documented during the 2025-03-14 admission for embolic cerebral infarction. CHA2DS2-VASc 5: female sex 1, age 65-74 1, hypertension 1, prior stroke 2. Guideline recommends oral anticoagulation. No anticoagulant is ordered - current medications per the 2026-07-10 clinic note are carvedilol, metoprolol tartrate and famotidine only, and no anticoagulant appears anywhere in the medication record. Needs review for initiation of anticoagulation for secondary stroke prevention.

Outside-records summary of 2026-08-12 documents an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 to Mercy Hospital for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9, 2 units transfused) with apixaban held at discharge pending cardiology review. That review has not happened: at the 2026-08-20 clinic visit apixaban 5 mg twice daily was re-ordered (valid 2026-08-20 to 2026-12-28) and the note states 'continue current regimen', with concurrent aspirin 81 mg and clopidogrel 75 mg. A current anticoagulant (plus dual antiplatelet therapy) is therefore running despite a documented major GI bleed that was explicitly flagged as requiring review before resumption.

Two oral anticoagulants are current for this patient with paroxysmal/persistent atrial fibrillation. At the 2026-07-15 cardiology clinic visit the plan was to switch rivaroxaban to apixaban ('Switching anticoagulant from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage. Start apixaban 5 mg twice daily'), but rivaroxaban 20 mg daily was re-ordered the same day (valid 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-25) alongside the new apixaban 5 mg twice daily order (valid 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-26), and the note's own medication list shows both drugs. Rivaroxaban was never discontinued, so as of 2026-09-24 the patient has overlapping apixaban and rivaroxaban - a major bleeding hazard requiring immediate reconciliation.

The clinic note of 2026-06-10 10:55 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that same day contradict this: 107914094 (2026-06-10 17:13) shows an irregularly irregular rhythm at a mean ventricular rate of about 133/min with no discernible P waves, and 103088543 (2026-06-10 19:36) shows the same at about 136/min - i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, not sinus rhythm at 72. Unspecified atrial fibrillation was in fact coded at the 2026-06-10/12 encounter and warfarin was started. The documented rhythm and rate need correction and the rate-control/anticoagulation plan re-reviewed.
